items.title: ‘FINAL FANTASY XIV Online’ Free Log-in Campaign Begins, “Up to 30 Days”
items.summary: This week, publisher SQUARE ENIX announced that, as part of their "The Road to Evercold" promotion for their critically acclaimed and long-running MMORPG
items.content:
Because you're not doing anything better anyways.

News Nintendo PC PlayStation Xbox Genghis Husameddin

This week, publisher SQUARE ENIX announced that, as part of their “The Road to Evercold” promotion for their critically acclaimed and long-running MMORPG title ‘FINAL FANTASY XIV Online’, lapsed players who have not had game time in their accounts for 150 days will be eligible to play “up to 30 days free” until 14 January 2027. This gives players a chance to catch up to the next expansion “Evercold”, with what people are calling “Shadowbringers 2”. A letter from the game’s producer YoshiP (Naoki Yoshida) regarding this latest promotion can be found here as well . This offer is primarily targeted for players who have already graduated from the game’s free trial status—simply log into the game client ( Windows / macOS (there is a better client out there for macOS BTW but I can’t link it)) and enjoy! Specific steps can be found below:

Details of service accounts can be confirmed via the FINAL FANTASY XIV: Mog Station . If you have never used Mog Station before, I apologise in advance. This offer works on consoles as well!

FINAL FANTASY XIV Online is available on PC via Steam/Mogstation, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch 2, and Xbox Series consoles —a free trial is available across all platforms, allowing newcomers to experience a now even more significant portion of FFXIV’s content for free (with a few restrictions). Without the trial, Xbox and Nintendo Switch players will need both an active subscription to FINAL FANTASY XIV Online and Xbox Live Gold/Game Pass/Nintendo Online to play the game. The game has more than 35 million registered accounts to date , showing the power of this critically acclaimed MMO and its parent franchise. FINAL FANTASY XIV Online: Evercold is slated for release on 23 February 2027.

items.title: "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat" - Square Enix tempts Final Fantasy 14 players back with free game-time to fill void before new expansion
items.summary: FF14 producer Naoki Yoshida says retaining active players is of "utmost importance", as Square Enix tempts players back with free game time.
items.content:
"People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons."

Image credit: Square Enix News by Connor Makar Reporter Published on Nov. 17, 2026, 11:48 a.m. 3 comments Follow Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold Prioritise us on Google Final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February. So, in order to keep the game populated for the next few months, Square Enix is running a special promotion in hopes of tempting players back in.

This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies. Lapsed players who haven't logged in for over six months are to be given 30 days of free game time to hop back in and catch up with the main story quest ahead of Evercold's release.

In addition, there's an alluring character skip available too. If your FF14 character is at least level 90 on one class - the current level-cap is 100 - you can skip all the way to the final part of the latest Dawntrail expansion. You still need to grind to level 100 in preparation for Evercold, but the aforementioned free month of game time should provide plenty of time to do so.

In a producer letter written to accompany this promotion , Naoki Yoshida provided insight into why this was being implemented, stating that retaining players in an MMO like FF14 was of the "utmost importance".

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat", Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

"For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn launched, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today."

Yoshida went on to explain that promotions such as this are meant as a "tiny nudge". He notes that those who have retained subscriptions continuously remain "the most important" players in the development team's eyes, and acknowledges that the process of catching up in an MMO can seem "daunting" for many.

This problem of player retention is nothing new for MMOs, especially in the tricky time between the end of a current expansion and the beginning of a new one. MMO popularity often waxes and wanes, with a new expansion acting as an exciting call to action, with the months leading up to it often serving as a natural break-point for many. Still, monthly subs pay the bills, so keeping folks around even during these quiet months is important.

Final Fantasy 14: Evercold is looking like an especially exciting expansion. On top of the new story and two classes being added, the game is getting an overhaul to combat, with both classic Reborn and Evolved action modes, as well as a new raid difficulty meant to bridge the gap between normal and savage tiers.

The game has certainly come a long way since its initial release back in 2010. Dawntrail proved divisive among fans too , though with Evercold there's a lot of hope that a new overarching storyline can bring the steal back the hearts of players old and new.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Players Get 30 Days of Free Game Time Before New Expansion
items.summary: "The Road to Evercold is a way to encourage any Warrior of Light currently taking a break to jump back in before the new expansion arrives," Naoki Yoshida stated in his Letter from the Producer.
items.content:
"The Road to Evercold is a way to encourage any Warrior of Light currently taking a break to jump back in before the new expansion arrives," Naoki Yoshida stated in his Letter from the Producer.

Every Final Fantasy XIV player will get a 30-day free game time ahead of the release of the new expansion, Evercold. As game director and producer Naoki Yoshida stated in his Letter from the Producer , it's the team's "way to encourage any Warrior of Light currently taking a break to jump back in before the new expansion arrives." It's the longest free login period offer, and the pre-Evercold generosity doesn't stop here.

Since Dawntrail became known as arguably the worst Final Fantasy expansion , many players left unwilling to continue the story. With Evercold, however, Square Enix is looking to bring back as many users as possible. Knowing how many of them have conflicting feelings (to say the least) about Dawntrail, they added a $9 cash shop item that will allow you to skip Endwalker's patch story along with the entirety of Dawntrail.

While paid skips are not new to Final Fantasy, this one is drastically different from the rest. Previously, paid skips stopped at the latest expansion, not allowing you to buy your way through the current story. This is the first time you'll be able to leave the ongoing expansion untouched and jump right into Evercold once it arrives.

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat. People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed," Yoshida confessed .

After Dawntrail made so many players leave the game, it seems like Square Enix decided to do as much as possible by the next expansion to win back a significant portion of users. With the release of Evercold, a number of major updates are coming to Final Fantasy XIV, and they'll be available to all players, including those who don't purchase Evercold. We'll see a new battle system, PvP updates, Duty Support updates, and housing updates.

"With the theme of evolution at the forefront, we're expanding and adjusting systems, user interfaces, and content in a way we've never attempted before. My biggest wish is that players currently taking a break will see Evercold as the perfect time to return," said Yoshida.

If this sounds intriguing to you and you want to take advantage of the 30-day free login campaign, you need to make sure you meet the following requirements:

The campaign runs from Monday, November 16, 2026, to Thursday, January 14, 2027. The release of Evercold is scheduled for Tuesday, February 23, 2027.

items.title: A paid Final Fantasy XIV item lets you skip Dawntrail
items.summary: Square Enix has introduced a rather surprising new item in its MMORPG’s in-game store. Final Fantasy XIV fans can now purchase Tales of Adventure: Winter’s…
items.content:
Square Enix has introduced a rather surprising new item in its MMORPG’s in-game store. Final Fantasy XIV fans can now purchase Tales of Adventure: Winter’s Prelude.

This item, which costs €6.99 , automatically completes the main story quests from Newfound Adventures (Update 6.1) through Into the Mist (Update 7.4). To be clear, this means players can thus completely skip the story of the Dawntrail expansion, which had received a rather lukewarm reception from fans. This will allow them to dive straight into the most recent content before the release of Evercold on February 23.

To use this item, you must have reached level 90, have access to all of the game’s expansions, and have completed the Endwalker quest.

items.title: Wisdom of Nym: Unanswered questions I have about Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold
Final Fantasy 14 really wants Evercold to be the expansion everyone comes back to, so much so it's giving you 30 days free gametime if you've been gone long enough
items.summary: Time to finish up that post-Dawntrail MSQ, folks.
items.content:
RPG Final Fantasy Final Fantasy 14 Final Fantasy 14 really wants Evercold to be the expansion everyone comes back to, so much so it's giving you 30 days free gametime if you've been gone long enough News By Mollie Taylor Published 16 November 2026 Time to finish up that post-Dawntrail MSQ, folks.

(Image credit: Square Enix) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Final Fantasy 14 is set to make some big changes when the upcoming expansion Evercold releases in February. An overhaul to combat, dailies, and new raid difficulties are set to shake things up and, hopefully, keep people sticking around for longer.

And judging by a recent Letter from the Producer , Naoki Yoshida really wants folks coming back to see what Evercold is all about. So much so that the game's offering 30 free days for long-gone adventurers… or a quick-and-dirty paid skip if you're so inclined.

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat," Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed."

I can only assume that for that reason, the decision's been made to offer up a $9 cash shop item that'll skip you through Endwalker's patch story, as well as all of Dawntrail up until the final story patch. Now Final Fantasy 14 has offered paid story skips in the past—it still does—but this is the first time it's explicitly offered one for the current expansion. Usually the skips'll stop dead before the current expansion, meaning you still need to play through the newest story.

It's a pretty niche paid skip, too. You'll need to have at least completed Endwalker's main story and have a level 90 job on your chosen character, and even then you'll still have to level up to 100 in your own time in order to tackle the final patch quest of Dawntrail. But worry not, if you haven't played the game in six months, you'll be able to snap up 30 days of free game time until January 14. Plenty of time to get a job to max level and prepare for Evercold.

Final Fantasy 14's ongoing pursuit in making its 500-hour story less daunting almost manifested into something in August, but Yoshi-P decided to postpone it Final Fantasy 14: Dawntrail's final story patch is exactly what the game needed, and has the 4-month wait for Evercold suddenly feeling a whole lot longer Final Fantasy 14: Evercold delayed to February, preorders start next week I'm mostly surprised by the introduction of this paid item because Yoshida has long been rather protective of the game's story. Something he admits in this very same letter: "I strongly believe that FF14 is a story-driven MMORPG," he wrote. "On top of that, skipping it all means you likely won't be familiar with the battle system and therefore will become a burden for other players in multiplayer content."

I do find it a little funny that Yoshida is worried that story skippers will weigh others down in dungeons and the like—I've played many a level 100 dungeon with folks who have clearly played enough to understand how to play yet still can't press their buttons properly.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

But anyway, Yoshida does admit that there is a lot of story to get through. "The Hydaelyn and Zodiark saga alone encompasses five expansions' worth of content," he wrote. "And with Dawntrail marking the start of the second saga, plus the coming addition of Evercold, the story continues to unfold into something even larger."

It really does feel like Square Enix wants Evercold to mark a big resurgence for the game, one I really do hope pays off for the developer. I've been playing off-and-on since A Realm Reborn and have seen just about every evolution the game has taken, and also the ways it has stagnated over time. Its confidence in trying to draw people back has me excited for the changes that are coming.

items.title: FF14 Free Trial Extended To Lapsed Players Ahead Of Evercold
items.summary: In preparation for Evercold, Square Enix is giving away 30 days of free game time to eligible players and has a new item for purchase that'll let you skip Dawntrail
items.content:
If you are like me and haven’t played Final Fantasy XIV in a minute, now might be the time to jump back in and finally get through Dawntrail before the new expansion launches in 2027. Starting November 16, players who haven’t logged in to the paid MMORPG in the last five months (150 days specifically) are eligible for 30 days of free playtime.

Players have from November 16th to January 14, 2027 to claim their free 30 days, which means that, if you time it right, your free period will overlap with the launch of the $45 Evercold expansion on February 23. Square Enix has all the specifics here .

The Road to Evercold begins today, helping you prepare for the upcoming release of Evercold!

⭐ 30-day Free Login Campaign ⭐ Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude

— FINAL FANTASY XIV (@en.finalfantasyxiv.com) 2026-11-16T10:30:05.686Z

Digging into the details, it seems like Square Enix knows a lot of people (including me) lit out after Endwalker and haven’t been back to play the latest expansion, Dawntrail. In addition to offering free game time, Square Enix is also offering a new $10 Tales of Adventure item which lets players auto-skip main story quest content. It’s designed specifically to leap-frog players over Dawntrail stuff, taking them from the end of Endwalker to the beginning of “In Fate’s Footsteps,” this year’s Evercold -introducing 7.5 event patch.

It is powerfully seductive to pay $10 bucks to take the coward’s way out of Dawntrail . I’ve heard that expansion is just okay, and possibly even worth skipping. But I play Final Fantasy XIV for its story. It can’t always be Heavensward or Shadowbringers , sometimes there has to be a Stormblood in there and that’s okay. As I try to take advantage of the free game time, I’ll finally see Dawntrail for myself.

items.title: Yoshi P Gives a Sneak Peek at Evolved Mode Job Changes for ‘Final Fantasy 14: Evercold’
Final Fantasy XIV Evercold Delayed, New Release Date Announced at FFXIV Fan Fest
items.summary: The MMORPG's next expansion was set to launch shortly after the new year, but Warriors of Light will have to wait a bit longer.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV Evercold was set to launch sometime in January 2027, which was announced as part of its initial reveal back in April this year during the North American FFXIV Fan Fest. However, this next expansion for the critically acclaimed MMORPG has been delayed – FFXIV Evercold's release date is now February 23, 2027 (and February 19, 2027 for early access). This was announced alongside the new, full trailer / intro cinematic for Evercold at FFXIV Fan Fest in Japan, and was said to only be a four-week delay.

In typical FFXIV fashion, the third and final teaser trailer is the full opening cinematic for an expansion, and it kicked off the Japan Fan Fest keynote where director and producer Naoki Yoshida presented more details on new features, where the ongoing story is headed, and fundemental gameplay changes as FFXIV goes into version 8.0 alongside Evercold's launch.

Pre-orders for Evercold open on November 4, 2026 and will come with a Wind-up Kottr minion to summon and follow you around in the world and Halone's Earring which will boost the EXP you gain for Jobs under level 100 when equipped. The collector's edition comes with the Valhallar Odin mount, the Entreat Crystal emote, and the Crystal Skyltborg which looks like glam for the new Bastion Job's weapons. The physical collector's bundle has the Evercold art book, the Tapestry of the Fourth decoration, a Kottr plush, a keychain of the Ethos Metal, and the Warrior of Light Reaper figure.

Additionally, we got a glimpse of the second new Job coming to his new expansion. It's a ranged DPS called Zephyr, which rocks a crossbow as their primary weapon and commands an avian companion to provide support.

There's a lot coming to FFXIV Evercold in addition to a new world and main story including a Neon Genesis Evangelion crossover raid series (which got a new teaser trailer) , a Final Fantasy VII crossover raid series, a new Tank Job with Bastion, and much more. Be sure to check out my Dawntrail review as well to look back at the last expansion before heading into this new era for FFXIV.
